title: Backend: rehydrate jobs from disk at startup
description: jobs is a process-local dict in create_app. A server restart empties /api/jobs, 404s every job URL, and orphans completed models that are sitting on disk in the session folder with meta.json and output/. Deep-linking and resumability are impossible until this is fixed. Scan root/*/meta.json at startup and reconstruct job records, deriving status from the presence of output/model.glb.
acceptance_criteria: After a server restart, GET /api/jobs lists prior sessions and GET /api/jobs/{id} returns 200 with its artifacts.
close_reason: Delivered in be1b31b + 382313b. 319 tests pass; verified in headless Chromium against a real job.

title: Rerun a finished or failed job with one click
description: A failed job holds everything needed to retry it: the staged photos in input/ (already renamed to carry view tags) and its settings. Nothing surfaced that. After an infrastructure failure -- stale SSH key, missing rtree -- the only way back was to re-upload the photos and re-pick every option. Persist the settings to session.json so a restored job can be rerun too, add POST /api/jobs/{id}/rerun, and put a button on the job detail screen.
close_reason: Shipped: POST /api/jobs/{id}/rerun creating a new session from the original's photos and settings, settings persisted to session.json so restored jobs are rerunnable, shared _register_and_dispatch with create_job, and controls on the job detail header plus every terminal row in the jobs list. 7 tests, verified end to end against a live server.

title: Worker image was missing rtree, killing the bake and the whole job
description: trimesh calls ProximityQuery.on_surface -> nearby_faces -> mesh.triangles_tree -> rtree, so the normal-map bake needs rtree even though nothing imports it directly. pixiecad-hunyuan in worker-v2 did not have it. The bake raised, and because unwrap and bake shared one try block the pipeline discarded a finished 969k-face mesh that had cost 333s of L4 time.
close_reason: Fixed in c85fb72. rtree installed into the live host image and into setup_hunyuan_vm.sh; launch_from_image.sh self-heal generalised to check_dep covering fast_simplification and rtree. Separately, unwrap and bake are no longer in one try block, so a bake failure can never discard a finished mesh again.

title: A GPU backend that cannot be reached must say why
description: A stale SSH HostKeyAlias in ~/.ssh/config (VM recreated, same name and IP, new instance id) made ssh fail host-key verification. RemoteHunyuanBackend.available() catches Exception and returns False, and SSHExecutor.probe() discards ssh stderr, so the job log said only: "Backend 'hunyuan-remote' is not available. Registered backends: ['fake','hunyuan-remote','trellis-remote']" -- which reads as a wrong backend NAME and sends you looking in the wrong place. The fix (gcloud compute config-ssh) was one command once the cause was visible. Surface the real reason: unreachable + ssh stderr, no GPU detected, or insufficient VRAM.
close_reason: Fixed in 95fcac3: Capabilities.detail + why_not(), probe() keeps ssh stderr, _ssh_hint() names the fix, available() records last_unavailable_reason, get_backend() prefers it over the registry dump. 15 new tests. The triggering incident was resolved by 'gcloud compute config-ssh' after the VM was recreated.

title: Texture stage: missing fast_simplification in the paint image
description: Sixth dependency failure in the Hunyuan paint stack. hy3dpaint/utils/simplify_mesh_utils.py calls trimesh.simplify_quadric_decimation, which in trimesh 4.x delegates to fast_simplification rather than a built-in. The package was never installed, so texturing dies with ModuleNotFoundError after the pipeline has already loaded (~15s GPU time) and the job finishes untextured with only a WARNING. Fixed in scripts/setup_hunyuan_texture.sh; the currently-baked machine image still lacks it and needs a rebake.
acceptance_criteria: A texture job on a freshly built image completes and reports 'Texture applied.'
notes: VM pixiecad-gpu self-destructed before the fix could be applied: launch_from_image.sh sets --max-run-duration=7200s with --instance-termination-action=DELETE, so every VM and its 200GB disk are deleted after exactly 2 hours. Nothing left to rebake from. Mitigation: launch_from_image.sh now checks the paint image for fast_simplification on every launch and patches it in place (~20s) if missing, so a stale machine image degrades to a slower launch rather than silently broken texturing. Rebake opportunistically during the next session, before the 2h timer.
close_reason: Fixed three ways: added to setup_hunyuan_texture.sh for future builds, self-healing patch in launch_from_image.sh for stale images, and baked into pixiecad-worker-v2. Verified in the image: fast_simplification 0.1.13.

title: Dashboard never writes output/model.glb
description: A completed dashboard run leaves only model_web.glb and parts/ in output/. The publish step copies the pipeline's glb (named <spec>.glb, e.g. tetrapod.glb) to output/model.glb, and finishing then rewrites it, but no job has ever produced that file. The full-resolution model is therefore only reachable inside work/ws/output/. Reproduce with a dashboard run and trace the publish block against finish_model's out_dir.
close_reason: Not reproducible: current code writes output/model.glb correctly (verified with a fake-backend run producing model.glb + model_web.glb + parts). My original diagnosis printed job['glb_path'], a field get_job never returns - it exposes glb_url. Kept a files API that lists output/ from disk so this class of confusion cannot recur.

title: Semantic part segmentation via multi-view 2D segmentation
description: Hunyuan output is a single fused shell (99.96% of area in one connected component), so connected-component splitting finds nothing and the pipeline falls back to k-means clustering, which carves arbitrary spatial blobs instead of semantic parts. Fix: render the mesh from N angles with a face-ID buffer, segment each RGB render with SAM on the GPU host, back-project masks to faces via the ID buffer, and fuse labels across views by voting.

title: Docker-created cache files are root-owned, breaking the TRELLIS token write
description: Containers run as root, so files docker creates in ~/.cache/huggingface are root-owned, and a machine image bakes that in. trellis_remote copies an HF token to ~/.cache/huggingface/token as the SSH user and fails with 'Permission denied' -- a message that says nothing about ownership. Fixed on the live host and self-healed at launch in launch_from_image.sh. A better fix is running the containers with --user, or keeping the token outside the shared cache.

Moves 3.4GB and ~14s off the 16GB dev machine. Note this is remote CPU, not GPU acceleration -- Blender GPU baking would be a separate, larger change.

The TRELLIS path, and everything gated behind DINOv3, is dormant. Revisit only if switching backends. 2026-08-04: the fal.ai backend was removed entirely, so trellis-remote is now the only alternative to hunyuan-remote -- if hunyuan ever has to be replaced, this bug is the first thing in the way.

value: Dashboard frontend is a React 19 + TS + Vite SPA in frontend/, built by 'npm run build' into src/pixiecad/web/static/dist/ (gitignored - rebuild after checkout or / falls back to the legacy page). Served at /ui with SPA fallback; / redirects there; the old single-file dashboard survives at /legacy. Hand-rolled ~70-line router (lib/router.ts) instead of react-router: 3 routes, drawer state in the query string. Two shared refcounted polling stores (lib/vm.ts, lib/jobs.ts) - never add a third poll of the same endpoint. Backend contract additions: jobs rehydrate from session.json at startup, GET /api/jobs/{id} returns stages[] and honours ?log_since=N. Verify UI changes with chrome-headless-shell from ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright (--dump-dom + --screenshot); it has NO WebGL, so the 3D viewer always takes its no-WebGL fallback path there.

Normal-map baking is the heaviest local stage in PixieCAD by two orders of magnitude. Measured 2026-08-04 on the 16GB M3 against a 1.31M-face source decimated to 20k: 512=6.0s/1.76GB, 1024=13.6s/3.4GB, 2048=52.9s/4.1GB, versus ~247MB for every other local stage combined. Profiling: the mesh itself is only 321MB; essentially all of it is ONE call, trimesh ProximityQuery.on_surface, and CHUNKING THAT QUERY DOES NOT HELP (peak stayed 6.5GB) -- do not retry that. Fix was to move the work: bake_location=auto|local|host, with meshops/bake_remote.py running the same bake.py inside the hunyuan container. Payload is compressed .npz (11.7MB), NOT .glb -- a GLB round-trip must carry UVs through TextureVisuals and losing them yields a plausible but wrong map. The remote bake does NO GPU work (runs without --gpus); it is remote CPU. Never yet run against a real GPU host.

The fal.ai backend was REMOVED on 2026-08-04 (pixiecad-cag). It offered hosted TRELLIS.2 with no VM/L4/gated-weights, but only by uploading the user's photos to a third party -- the exact thing building Hunyuan from Tencent's own source was meant to avoid. It had never produced a model here. AUTO_PRIORITY is now [hunyuan-remote, trellis-remote]; there is no hosted backend and no FAL_KEY anywhere. tests/test_web.py::TestBackendSelection::test_no_third_party_hosted_backend_is_offered asserts none can reappear in the registry or the auto order, because the failure mode is silent: a job would just start uploading.

The Hunyuan worker image needs rtree, though nothing imports it directly: trimesh reaches it via ProximityQuery.on_surface -> nearby_faces -> mesh.triangles_tree -> rtree, which the normal-map bake calls. Missing it in pixiecad-worker-v2 killed a job AFTER 333s of L4 generation. Now in setup_hunyuan_vm.sh and in launch_from_image.sh's check_dep self-heal (alongside fast_simplification for the paint image). Remote bake measured 45.5s at 1024 end-to-end on g2-standard-16 -- SLOWER than the 13.6s local bake; the reason to use the host is the 3.4GB of local RAM, not speed.

The TRELLIS image is built with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9 and no +PTX, so it ships Ada cubins only. A T4 (7.5), A100 (8.0) and H100 (9.0) all fail at kernel launch regardless of VRAM. L4 is the required GPU; availability checks must test compute capability, not just VRAM.

Hunyuan3D paint (texture) stack: bpy MUST be 4.2.x (oldest cp311 wheel; 5.x is cp312) and needs libxkbcommon0/libsm6/libice6/libxxf86vm1/libxfixes3/libxrandr2/libxinerama1/libxcursor1 even headless. basicsr needs functional_tensor->functional patched via find+sed (importing basicsr to locate it is what fails). Run the container with -w /opt/hunyuan (configs are relative to repo root) and pin realesrgan_ckpt_path absolutely. CRITICAL: end the script with os._exit(code) -- bpy teardown returns non-zero after a clean run, so a fully successful job reads as failed. 123s on an L4 for 2048x2048 PBR maps.

L4 spot is persistently stocked out in all three asia-south1 zones (verified twice, 2026-08-02). asia-southeast1-b has capacity. L4 quota is 1 on-demand + 1 spot in every region checked, so sweep zones for spot rather than paying ~4x for on-demand.

Part segmentation on a fused generative mesh: render 14 views keeping a face-id buffer, run SAM per view, vote on mesh EDGES (agree minus disagree across views), then Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher with k/area to form regions. Two designs failed first: clustering masks (SAM splits a wheel into rim+tyre in one view -> 90+ fragments) and cut-then-merge-by-mean-agreement (snowballs, one region went 13.6%->97.9%). Adjacency MUST be UV-seam-aware (_positional_face_adjacency); mesh.face_adjacency left 390 regions with no neighbour. SAM vit_h on a T4 = 125s for 14 views at 768px.

Spot is a bad fit for the TRELLIS leg specifically: ~15min cold start (9GB image pull + 19GB model download) and preemption DELETEs the boot disk, losing the whole cache. One run was preempted 8 min in. COLMAP dense is fine on spot because it is short and the stage cache absorbs a restart.

TRELLIS.2 requires an HF token: it loads facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m which is a GATED repo. The 401 only surfaces AFTER downloading 19GB and several minutes of loading, so always check the token before provisioning. Accept licence at huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m, then export HF_TOKEN.

DINOv3 ViT-L/16 weights are secured locally. HF gate for facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m is APPROVED on this account (config.json returns 200). Two copies: the live HF cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--facebook--dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m) which is what any tool resolves automatically, and a purge-proof archive at ~/models/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m (1.21 GB, cp -RL so no dangling symlinks, SHA256SUMS alongside: model.safetensors = dcb2e45127cccbf1601e5f42fef165eea275c8e5213197e8dcf3f48822718179). LICENSE.md from Meta ships in both. No re-request needed ever; approval also persists on the HF account. NOTE: these weights are for TRELLIS.2 only, which is NOT on the live path -- AUTO_PRIORITY puts hunyuan-remote first and it always wins.

SSH host-key gotcha on this project: recreating a GPU VM with the SAME name often reuses the external IP, but ~/.ssh/config still pins the OLD instance's HostKeyAlias (written by gcloud compute config-ssh), so plain ssh fails host-key verification with rc=255 while 'gcloud compute ssh' keeps working -- it manages that mapping itself. Symptom before the 2026-08-04 fix: 'Backend hunyuan-remote is not available. Registered backends: [...]', which points at the wrong thing entirely. Fix: gcloud compute config-ssh. Verified the key change was benign by comparing instance ids, not by blindly clearing known_hosts.

TRELLIS load-time host RAM: OOM-killed at 15.2GB on g2-standard-4 (16GB); still climbing past 28GB on g2-standard-8 (32GB). Use g2-standard-16 (64GB). Adding swap makes it worse - paging a model load onto pd-balanced wedges the VM entirely.

Hunyuan3D multi-view (2mv) is WORSE than single-view 2.1 on the F1 set: 2mv merged the front wheels into a slab and gave 18 components vs 5 for single-view, which kept four distinct wheels. Swapping left/right views changed nothing, so it is not a tag-convention issue -- 2mv is built on the older 2.0 line. Default is single-view 2.1; --multiview is opt-in.

S0 ingest is nowhere near needing cloud offload: the entire local pipeline (ingest, clean, decimate, UV unwrap, normal bake, parts export) peaks at 247 MB RSS in 1.9s on 8 1024px images. Only S2b dense stereo and S3 generative need a GPU host.

TRELLIS worker image kngsly/trellis2-worker is a FastAPI SERVICE (CMD python server.py, EXPOSE 8000), not a CLI. Protocol: GET /ready, POST /generate multipart with repeated 'images' fields returning an NDJSON stream whose last frame carries success+glb_path, GET /download/<name>. Bind-mount /outputs to read the glb straight off the host instead of downloading it.
